title: Where can you fly direct from Exeter Airport?
author: Matt
intro: Exeter is a small airport with a useful mix of routes: TUI holidays to the Mediterranean and the Canaries, Ryanair to Spain, KLM to Amsterdam, and short hops to Scotland and the Channel Islands. Here's what flies from Exeter, when, and how to get further afield.
seo_title: Where can you fly direct from Exeter? (2026 guide)
seo_description: TUI, Ryanair, KLM, Loganair and Aurigny fly from Exeter: Canaries winter sun, Med beach holidays, Amsterdam and the Channel Islands. Checked Nov 2026.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Main airlines:** TUI, Ryanair and KLM
- **Winter sun:** the Canaries with TUI
- **New for 2027:** Ryanair to Porto
- **Long-haul:** connect via Amsterdam

We checked these routes in November 2026 from airline and airport announcements. Exeter's timetable changes a lot between summer and winter, and some routes run only a day or two a week, so check the airline's own schedule before you plan a trip around one. Flight times are typical and vary with the wind.

sections.heading: Who flies from Exeter
sections.text:
| Airline | Where it flies | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TUI | Canaries, Greece, Spain, Cyprus, Turkey | most in summer, Canaries in winter |
| Ryanair | Alicante, Málaga, Porto from 2027 | Málaga all year |
| KLM | [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) | all year |
| Loganair | [Edinburgh](/destinations/edinburgh), Jersey | all year, check days |
| Aurigny | Guernsey | all year, check days |

TUI is the biggest holiday airline at Exeter, and its package holidays make up much of the summer schedule. Loganair has cut back here recently: its Manchester route ended in August 2026 and Newcastle ended on 25 October 2026. Loganair still lists Glasgow from Exeter too, so check its booking page for current days.

sections.heading: Winter sun
sections.text:
From November to February, TUI flies from Exeter to the Canary Islands, the warmest beach weather within easy reach of the UK in winter:

- **[Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife):** about 4¼ hours, around 22°C by day in winter.
- **[Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote):** about 4 hours, calmer and drier, around 21 to 22°C.
- **[Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria):** about 4¼ hours, with the sunniest resorts in the south.

Ryanair's [Málaga](/destinations/malaga) flights run all year too, at about two and a half hours. In winter it's mild rather than hot, at around 17 to 18°C, but good for a sunny long weekend.

Tip: Exeter's winter flights often go only once or twice a week, so your trip length may be set by the flight days. Check the days before you pick a hotel.

sections.heading: Summer beach holidays
sections.text:
In summer, TUI adds most of the classic Mediterranean holiday spots:

- **Spain:** [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca) and [Menorca](/destinations/menorca), about 2¼ hours.
- **Greece:** [Corfu](/destinations/corfu), [Crete](/destinations/crete), [Rhodes](/destinations/rhodes) and [Zante](/destinations/zakynthos), about 3 to 4 hours.
- **Cyprus:** [Paphos](/destinations/paphos), about 4½ hours, listed on Wednesdays and Saturdays for 2027.
- **Turkey:** Dalaman, twice a week in 2027, and [Antalya](/destinations/antalya), about 4 hours.

Ryanair's Alicante flights add the Costa Blanca, at about 2¼ hours. Most of these routes run from around May to October, so check the season dates if you're planning an early or late trip. Our [beach holidays](/destinations/beach-holidays) page compares the best beaches by month.

sections.heading: City breaks and short hops
sections.text:
Exeter doesn't have many city routes, but the ones it has are useful:

- **[Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam):** KLM, about 1¼ hours, all year. It's a great weekend in itself and the easiest way to connect onwards.
- **[Porto](/destinations/porto):** new with Ryanair from 30 March 2027, on Tuesdays and Saturdays, about 2 hours.
- **[Edinburgh](/destinations/edinburgh):** Loganair, about 1½ hours, much quicker than the train.
- **Jersey and Guernsey:** Loganair to Jersey and Aurigny to Guernsey, both short flights of under an hour.

In summer, Skybus has also flown from Exeter to St Mary's on the Isles of Scilly, so check its timetable if you want an island break closer to home. For more ideas, see our [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page.

sections.heading: Long-haul and connections
sections.text:
There are no regular direct long-haul flights from Exeter. TUI's Barbados fly-cruise on 9 December 2027 is a one-off cruise departure, not a holiday flight you can book on its own.

For anywhere further, the easiest routes are:

- **Connect in Amsterdam with KLM.** You can book through to its worldwide network on one ticket, and your bags usually go all the way.
- **Fly from Bristol**, about an hour and a half up the M5, for more European routes. See [where you can fly direct from Bristol](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-bristol-airport).
- **Fly from Heathrow or Gatwick** for the widest choice of direct long-haul flights. Heathrow is about three hours by road.

Watch out: if you connect on separate tickets, a late first flight can mean a missed second one with no rebooking. Booking through on one ticket is safer.

sections.heading: Getting to Exeter Airport
sections.text:
The airport is about five miles east of Exeter city centre, just off the A30 and close to junction 29 of the M5.

- **Driving:** most people drive, and booking parking ahead is usually cheaper than paying on the day.
- **Bus or taxi:** both run from the city, so check current times if you're on an early flight.

It's a small, quick airport, but it gets busy when several holiday flights leave in the same morning. Our guide to [how early to arrive at Exeter Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-exeter-airport) covers check-in and security times.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Exeter?
sections.text:
For winter sun, start with [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) or [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote). For summer, [Corfu](/destinations/corfu), [Crete](/destinations/crete) and [Menorca](/destinations/menorca) are all easy from Exeter, and [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) or [Porto](/destinations/porto) make good weekends away.

If you're choosing as a family or group, put the Exeter routes you like on a shared list in somewhere.party, give everyone points to vote with, and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Which airlines fly from Exeter Airport?
faqs.answer: TUI, Ryanair and KLM fly the main routes, with Loganair to Edinburgh and Jersey and Aurigny to Guernsey. Routes and days change by season, so check each airline's timetable.

faqs.question: Can you fly to the Canaries from Exeter in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes. TUI flies from Exeter to Tenerife, Lanzarote and Gran Canaria in winter, usually once or twice a week to each island. The flight takes about four to four and a quarter hours.

faqs.question: Are there long-haul flights from Exeter?
faqs.answer: Not regular ones. The easiest way to fly long-haul from Exeter is to connect through Amsterdam with KLM, or to fly from Heathrow or Gatwick.

faqs.question: Is there a new route from Exeter in 2027?
faqs.answer: Ryanair is adding Porto from 30 March 2027, twice a week on Tuesdays and Saturdays, according to the airport's announcement.
